E1.excerpt: Here we report a nickel stabilized ruthenium dioxide (Ni-RuO2) catalyst, a promising alternative to iridium, with high activity and durability in acidic OER for PEM water electrolysis.

E2.excerpt: In the format provided by the authors and unedited

E3.excerpt: a 4e- OER on RuO2 (110) starts from H2O adsorption at a CUS Ru site, followed by two sequential deprotonation steps to form *OH and then *O

E4.where: main: Synthesis and characterizations of catalysts (Supplementary Fig. 1c) … main: Mechanism understanding
E4.excerpt: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Ni-RuO2 showed the characteristic peaks of rutile RuO2 (JCPDS 71-2273) with the dominant (110) peak at 28.1° … Consistent with our XRD observation (Supplementary Fig. 1c), RuO2 crystal was modelled to have a rutile lattice structure.

E5.excerpt: we chose to study the catalytic properties of fully oxidized (110) surface of RuO2 (Fig. 4a and Supplementary Fig. 34a)

E6.excerpt: The OER limiting potential, defined as the lowest potential under which the free energy evolution becomes downhill, is about 1.89 V on RuO2 (110) surface.

note: Two rutile RuO2(110) models: pristine RuO2(110) (reported, UL=1.89 V) and Ni-doped RuO2(110) (UL=1.70 V), both all-YES. E2 UNCLEAR: no publication date printed in main text or SI.
